chapter: Benny Carter, saxophones and Coleman Hawkins's last years
title: Ben Webster switches from a Conn to a Selmer saxophone
summary: Caldwell coached Webster through the unfamiliar Selmer, whose tone carries farther than it sounds under the player's ear.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: No, Benny's always ready to come down -- funny thing, before we started playing the Selmer saxophone, I done had a Conn, and he had a Conn. So over at that little place across from the Savoy called the Bridgeport, downstairs, Ben always said, I like what you're playing, Hap. I said, well, this is western style, (unintelligible) trying to come out of the West. He says, yeah. So he said, I'm going to get another saxophone. I said, good, said, what are you going to get?

He said, Selmer. Well, the Selmer's peculiar instrument. If not like the Conn, the Conn you -- when you play it, (unintelligible) you could hear it right on top of you, but when you're playing the Selmer, you're supposed to think you're playing loud, but the tone goes, has the carrying power. That's the way it's constructed.
But I mean the shape is the same.
You right -- that's right. But if you're not accustomed to it, you got to get accustomed to it. He said, damn, he said, I don't hear it like I did on the Conn.
Well, isn't the metal a little heavier or --

Well, the are (unintelligible) I just traded in in July. That was the balanced action, and, of course, Hawk had this. Ben had this; that's what I had after (unintelligible) my Conn. So he used to come down with the Selmer. Well, I said, Bill what are you going to do? He said, man, said, I can't play this thing, said, I'm used to playing the Conn like you are. I said, well, you want to try that? I says, I don't care, but I picked the horn up and started playing it. He said, well, how the hell did you do that? I said, well, I don't know, Ben. I said, I know the fingering is closer than it is on the Conn, I said, but I was just -- sometimes you can do things you don't realize what you're doing.

I said, you take this horn back and leave the Conn. I says, you got to get used to playing the horn. So Duke was playing at the Savoy. So he said, man, I don't know I can do that. I said, you got to do it, Benny, if you want to learn to play the Selmer. I says, you got to get accustomed to it. I said, because what you hear and what I hear on the Conn (unintelligible).

I'm going to blow this Selmer. Now, you get in the back, and you'll hear the difference. And he did. He said, Jesus, said, I can hear you clear back there. I said, so I can hear you clear back there, when you play the Selmer. The tone goes.
But you never could figure out --

And so he said, gee whiz, said, you showed me something. I said, leave the Conn here and take the Selmer with you, and by the time you come back off the road after you make this trip, you'll have known what you want to do with the Selmer. Sure enough, he did. He came back, he said -- and he said, you were right.
Well, I mean actually most people switched to Selmer's, didn't they?
